title: The Morning Digest: November 2, 2026
dek: Brent Jan27, the new front contract, traded down to $109.75 in early Asian trade on Monday (QNA, Nov 2), down $3.68 from Friday's $113.43 settle, and WTI Dec26 traded down to $100.69, down $3.43 from $104.12, as Iranian and Qatari officials held a third day of talks on a two day reopening proposal for the Strait of Hormuz centred on the release of more than $6 billion of frozen Iranian funds. No agreement has been reached and no flow print has moved. OPEC+ formalised its December hold in a statement on Nov 1, maintaining September required production for December at a combined target of about 31.01 million barrels a day for the seven core members, with the next meeting on Nov 29 to set the 2027 framework. December WCS is -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots, November Mainline apportionment of Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert is in effect, and the validated diesel crack is $90.90.

sources.vintage: Nov 2, 2026 (early Asian trade Monday: Brent Jan27 down $3.68 or 3.2 percent to $109.75 at the low print reported by QNA from Singapore, with the Reuters 0011 GMT print at $111.84, down $1.59; WTI Dec26 down $3.43 or 3.3 percent to $100.69, with the Reuters 0011 GMT print at $102.56, down $1.56; Friday settles WTI Dec26 $104.12 and Brent Jan27 $113.43, with Brent Dec26 expiring at $117.64; the slide built as a third day of Iranian and Qatari talks in Doha was reported)

sources.publisher: Reuters, Gulf News and Guardian reporting
sources.vintage: Nov 1-2, 2026 (third consecutive day of talks in Doha; the reopening proposal shortened from seven days to two, with Washington to act on the first day on sanctions relief, frozen funds release and oil waivers and shipping to resume on the second; Qatar pushing release of more than $6 billion of frozen Iranian assets held in restricted Qatari accounts; Iran's foreign minister said Nov 1 the consultations had reached no conclusion and there are no plans for direct talks with Washington; Washington has said no decision has been made on renewed strikes; Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed two tankers hit mines on an unauthorised route through the strait, with no CENTCOM or UKMTO confirmation reported)

Nov 1, 2026 (seven core members decided to maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026, a third straight monthly hold; combined December target about 31.01 million barrels a day: Saudi Arabia 10.478, Russia 9.949, Iraq 4.431, Kuwait 2.676, Kazakhstan 1.628, Algeria 1.007, Oman 0.841; the 1.65 million barrel a day rollback completed in September; about 2 million barrels a day of further cuts run through the end of 2026; most members pump below target, with Saudi Arabia reporting September output of 8.372 million barrels a day to OPEC; next meeting Nov 29 to decide the 2027 framework)
